{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRkquM8AAAABZYOVMg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5zhC_lzs", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5", "number": 33, "title": "Reload HDMA descriptors and indirect pointers at row end", "body": "## Problem

HDMA reloads subsequent row metadata one HBlank too late. At baseline `edb25aaa2aff9bfe7022252bcb25fb15fa218d5d`, `hdma_events` fetches a descriptor before the next payload when the previous counter's low seven bits are zero. It also terminates on a zero descriptor before performing indirect-pointer reads. Consequently, CPU writes between HBlanks can incorrectly replace metadata that should already have been fetched, and termination omits observable table reads and pointer updates. See [the current implementation](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/edb25aaa2aff9bfe7022252bcb25fb15fa218d5d/crates/snes-core/src/machine.rs#L539).

This completes a bounded gap explicitly retained by [Issue #31's validation record](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/edb25aaa2aff9bfe7022252bcb25fb15fa218d5d/docs/issue-31-validation.md#timing-convention-and-retained-approximations). It does not duplicate that completed initialization-prefetch improvement. The supplied context lists no open Issues.

## Expected outcome

Implement subsequent-row reload and termination during the HBlank that finishes the preceding row, with metadata visible before CPU execution resumes.

Hardware contract:

- Transfer the current scanline's eligible payload using prepared metadata. Decrement line state once per serviced scanline, including scanlines that hold a nonrepeated value. When the decremented counter's low seven bits reach zero, fetch the next descriptor during this same HBlank. A nonzero descriptor prepares the next scanline; it must not cause another payload in the current HBlank.
- Publish the fetched descriptor in `$43xA` and advance `$43x8/9`. For indirect HDMA, fetch and publish the next little-endian address in `$43x5/6` during that reload. CPU edits afterward must not replace prepared metadata; payload bytes remain live until their transfer.
- Preserve repeat semantics: `$01/$81` end after one scanline; `$02` transfers once and holds for the second scanline; `$82` transfers on both scanlines. A freshly loaded `$80` represents 128 scanlines with one initial transfer followed by holds. Do not confuse a fresh `$80` with `$80` reached by decrementing `$81`, and do not immediately consume a freshly reloaded row.
- A zero descriptor terminates the channel internally without clearing its programmed `$420C` bit. Direct termination consumes the descriptor only. For indirect termination, the repository-recorded Anomie rule requires both pointer bytes when a later active channel remains; for the last active channel, zero supplies the pointer low byte and only the following table byte is fetched as high. Publish the resulting address and table progression even though no subsequent payload occurs.
- Descriptor and pointer fetches remain A-bus reads regardless of transfer direction. Preserve applicable read side effects and access restrictions. Table and payload addresses wrap within their respective 16-bit addresses without carrying into the bank. Preserve `$43x2/3/4/7` and existing payload-mode behavior.

Specification sources: [Anomie's Register Doc, revision 1157](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gilligan/snesdev/master/docs/snes_registers.txt), **43x0–43xA** and **DMA AND HDMA → HDMA**, especially the ordered transfer/reload algorithm and step 5b's terminating indirect read; [Fullsnes](https://problemkaputt.de/fullsnes.htm), **DMA and HDMA Channel 0..7 Registers** and **Notes**. [The repository's specification record](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/edb25aaa2aff9bfe7022252bcb25fb15fa218d5d/docs/issue-31-validation.md#specification-evidence-and-supported-state-transitions) identifies reference versions, hashes and relevant sections.

Evidence limit: this planning pass inspected repository evidence only. The ignored reference copies are unavailable here. Before fixing multi-channel expectations, check the cited ordered algorithm for payload-versus-reload phase order and exactly which channels count as later active during termination. Record the supporting text and derivation. Fullsnes is not recorded as independently confirming the zero-header quirk. If that check contradicts an earlier Issue contract, correct its affected implementation, tests and documentation with evidence; passing an earlier contract test is not grounds to preserve an unsupported requirement.

Scope is subsequent-row transitions, including channel ordering and termination effects necessary for those transitions. Retain frame-initialization prefetch. Non-goals are changing the 1096-master-clock HBlank convention, initialization/startup alignment or global overhead, arbitrary mid-frame enabling, same-channel DMA contention, electrical open-bus values, PAL/display modes, and unrelated refactoring.

## Context and reproduction

A minimal original scheduler vector can use direct mode 0, destination `$2140`, and a WRAM table at `$7E:0100`:

```text
81 11 82 22 33 00
```

Enable channel 0 before natural frame initialization and advance through its first HBlank.

Expected after that HBlank: destination received `$11`, `$43x8/9 == $0103`, and `$43xA == $82`; the second descriptor is already prepared. Current code instead leaves the table address at `$0102` and counter at `$80`.

Between that HBlank and the next, replace `$7E:0102` with zero and `$7E:0103` with `$66`. Expected next payload is live `$66` using the retained `$82` descriptor. Current code reads the replacement zero and terminates. Add an indirect counterpart that changes both the already-fetched pointer bytes and the original target's live payload.

Existing tests require source-backed expectation corrections. For example, [the complete-table conflict vector](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/edb25aaa2aff9bfe7022252bcb25fb15fa218d5d/crates/snes-core/src/machine/dma_tests.rs#L922) encodes delayed reload, and [the initialization/DMA overlap vector](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/edb25aaa2aff9bfe7022252bcb25fb15fa218d5d/crates/snes-core/src/machine/hdma_init_tests.rs#L170) expects `$80` after a row's final payload. Update obsolete metadata/timing expectations with explicit derivations while preserving their access, conflict, payload and device-progress coverage.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Implement the specified row-end transition in production code. Document reference-backed channel phase ordering and zero-termination read sequences, separating specification facts, derivations and retained scheduler approximations. Correct any contradicted earlier contract explicitly.
- [ ] Add original Rust scheduler regressions driven by natural initialization and HBlank events rather than injected pending/active/line state. Demonstrate baseline failure and final success for direct and indirect metadata edits between HBlanks, prepared-register visibility, and live payload reads.
- [ ] Cover `$01`, `$02`, `$80`, `$81`, `$82` and `$FF` row boundaries; reload after a held scanline; fresh `$80` loaded by a subsequent-row reload; and zero termination without an extra payload or delayed HBlank. Assert numeric destinations, counters, table addresses, indirect addresses and programmed versus internal channel state.
- [ ] Cover terminating indirect reads with and without a later active channel, including disabled and already-terminated later-channel controls and a later channel that also encounters zero during the same event. Distinguish the read sequences through addresses/register effects. Cover 16-bit table and payload wrap, both payload directions, and a status-register read-clear effect. Assert channel order according to the checked specification rather than implementation loop order.
- [ ] Add different-channel general-DMA overlap across a subsequent reload and termination. Require no lost or duplicated payloads, correct final DMA address/count, and continued raster/APU advancement. Charge actual metadata reads through the existing timed access path; do not describe aggregate emulator clocks as proven hardware alignment.
- [ ] Add bounded original direct/indirect 65C816 guests, for example `crates/snes-core/tests/hdma_reload.rs`, that configure during VBlank, synchronize through executed register reads, edit metadata between HBlanks, and record numeric register/destination results in WRAM. Host code supplies the cartridge and observes results without injecting execution state. Record original MIT instruction/data provenance in `tests/roms/PROVENANCE.md`; use no commercial ROM, firmware or unaudited binary.
- [ ] Preserve existing hardware-side-effect coverage and all game regressions. Any changed old assertion must be tied to the corrected row-end contract. Keep fixture pins/hashes, game inputs, frame counts, gameplay/audio checks and freeze controls intact.
- [ ] Pass the following pre-merge checks, using the README's toolchain selection where needed. Record actual results and baseline failures in a focused validation record:

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace --locked
cargo test --locked -p snes-core --lib machine::
cargo test --locked -p snes-core --test dma_access
cargo test --locked -p snes-core --test hdma_init
cargo test --locked -p snes-core --test hdma_reload
python3 tools/make-fixture.py .cache/smoke.bin
cmp tests/roms/smoke.bin .cache/smoke.bin
python3 tools/build-test-tools.py --spc
python3 tools/hardware-tests.py \
  --ca65 "$PWD/.cache/tools/cc65/bin/ca65" \
  --ld65 "$PWD/.cache/tools/cc65/bin/ld65" \
  --spcasm "$PWD/.cache/tools/spcasm/target/release/spcasm"
python3 tools/ppu-test.py --bass "$PWD/.cache/tools/bass-untech/bass/out/bass-untech"
python3 tools/build-cleared-games.py
python3 tools/build-cleared-games.py
npm --prefix web ci
npm --prefix web run build
(cd web && npx playwright install chromium)
npm --prefix web test -- --grep-invert '301 seconds'
```

These gates follow [README validation](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/edb25aaa2aff9bfe7022252bcb25fb15fa218d5d/README.md#validate) and preserve the source-built CPU/SPC/HDMA fixtures and cleared Castle/Memory browser regressions. Use the documented alternate browser port if necessary.

- [ ] Update limitations honestly. HDMA remains partial: startup/alignment/full overhead, arbitrary mid-frame enabling, same-channel contention, electrical behavior and the complete interaction matrix remain outstanding. Preserve every supplied inventory scope/status: partial `cpu`, `bus`, `scheduler`, `dma`, `hdma`, `controllers`, `ppu-bg`, `ppu-offset`, `ppu-mode7`, `ppu-objects`, `ppu-color`, `ppu-ports`, `ppu-display`, `spc`, `ipl`, `dsp-noise`, `dsp-pitch`, `dsp-envelope`, `dsp-echo`, `dsp-timing`; implemented_unverified `dsp-voices`; unimplemented `ppu-hires`, `ppu-raster`, `pal`. Limited test passes establish neither full hardware accuracy nor commercial compatibility.

## Optional validation

None. No tests were rerun during this read-only planning pass.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
